proof.observed: All eight cases answer exactly as they did before the merge. Accepted 201 with the anchor left on the original block: a heading's comment copied into the front matter (still on the heading) and an ask's quote copied into a code block above it (still open on the paragraph). Refused 400 INVALID_MARKDOWN: into a code block alone ('a code block ... out of it'), into the front matter alone ('the front matter'), into the front matter and a code block ('the front matter and a code block ... out of them'), into two separate code blocks ('two code blocks ... out of them'), into a code block where it stood and the front matter far above ('a code block and the front matter', nearest first), and into one code block holding the quote twice ('a code block ... out of it'). Every refusal leaves the artifact at version 1 with the anchor open and unorphaned, and no level=ERROR line is written in any of the eight.
proof.negativeControl: The refusals are themselves the control for the accepted pair, and the two accepted copies the control for the refusals: the same quote, the same anchor, the difference being only whether the upload leaves it somewhere its mark may stand. proof.criterion: The race skip fires only under the race detector, so acceptance 3's room-memory bounds are still measured in the normal build
proof.surface: the real docs.Service on a live room over its websocket on Postgres 16, built twice: once with the race detector and once without
proof.command: cd packages/envoy && CGO_ENABLED=1 GOMAXPROCS=4 DISPATCH_TEST_DATABASE_URL=… go test -race -p 2 -parallel 4 ./internal/dispatch/docs/ -run 'KeepMemoryWithinTheBound|KeepsMemoryWithinTheBound' -count=1 -v; then the same without -race, in the wider subset that also runs the anchor oracles and the refusal table
proof.observed: Under -race: --- SKIP for all three, 0.00 s each, package ok in 1.121 s. Without -race: all three run and pass - 200 one-token uploads 673 B per upload against 883 B stored; 250 writes 1,959 B per write against 927 B stored; 400 writes in the production mix 1,499 B per write against 2,088 B stored - each inside its stored-plus-2-MiB bound. proof.negativeControl: The non-race run is the control for the skip: if skipUnderRace fired on the ordinary build the three tests would report SKIP there too and acceptance 3 would be unmeasured. They report their bounds instead.
